questions.question: What does 'first + last coding' compute?
options: The sum of the alphabet positions of the word's first and last letters
The word's total length
The product of the first and last letters' positions
Only the first letter's position
questions.rationale: First + last coding adds together the alphabet-position values of just the word's first and last letters.

questions.question: What does 'first x last coding' compute, in contrast?
options: The same sum as first + last coding
The difference between them
The product of the alphabet positions of the word's first and last letters
The average of all letters in the word
questions.rationale: Instead of adding the first and last letters' positions, this variation multiplies them together to produce the code.

questions.question: What does 'first-last difference' compute?
options: The sum of the first and last letters' positions
The difference between the alphabet positions of the word's first and last letters
The word's total length
The average of all letters
questions.rationale: This computes the numeric gap (difference) between the alphabet positions of the word's first and last letters.

questions.question: What does 'middle-letter coding' use as a word's code?
options: The word's first letter
The total letter count
The word's last letter
The letter (or letters) positioned in the middle of the word
questions.rationale: Middle-letter coding bases the code on whichever letter (or letters, for even-length words) sits in the middle of the word.

questions.question: What is 'sentence coding'?
options: Applying a coding rule across an entire sentence rather than just a single word, often word by word
Coding that only works on single letters
A rule that ignores whole sentences
Only relevant to the Chinese coding method
questions.rationale: Sentence coding extends the coding logic beyond a single word, applying a rule across an entire sentence, typically transforming it word by word.

questions.question: What is the 'Chinese coding method' generally known for in coding-decoding reasoning?
options: A rule based on Chinese characters directly
A technique where each word in a sentence is assigned an arbitrary code word, and the mapping must be deduced from multiple coded sentences sharing common words
A synonym for letter-shift coding
A method that only uses numbers
questions.rationale: In this classic technique, whole words are replaced with arbitrary code words, and the solver must compare multiple coded sentences with overlapping real words to deduce which code word means what.

questions.question: What does the 'Chinese coding algorithm' involve as its core step?
options: Applying a single alphabet shift
Comparing multiple coded sentences to find which code word consistently corresponds to which real word, by process of elimination
Reversing every word in the sentence
Counting letters in each sentence
questions.rationale: The core technique is comparing several coded sentences that share common real words, using process of elimination to isolate which code word corresponds to which real word.

questions.question: Using first+last coding, what is the code for 'CAT' (C=3, T=20)?
Using first x last coding, what is the code for 'CAT' (C=3, T=20)?
Why does the Chinese coding method require comparing MULTIPLE coded sentences rather than just one?
options: One sentence is always sufficient
Because a single sentence only pairs whole coded sentences with whole real sentences; comparing several with overlapping words is needed to isolate which code corresponds to which individual word
Because Chinese coding never uses more than one sentence
Because multiple sentences are required only for very long words
questions.rationale: A single sentence pair only tells you which set of code words matches which set of real words as a whole — you need overlapping words across multiple sentences to isolate the mapping for each individual word.
